senses.sense_definition: A stiff petticoat or structure of hoops worn under a woman's skirt to hold it out in a wide bell shape.

examples.text: The actress wore an elaborate Victorian gown supported by a wide <w>crinoline</w> beneath.
It was difficult for women to walk through narrow doorways while wearing a voluminous <w>crinoline</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A dress or skirt supported by hoops to create an expansive, voluminous silhouette.

examples.text: Dancers whirled across the ballroom in colorful silk <w>crinolines</w> that swished with every step.
Historical paintings from the mid-nineteenth century frequently depict ladies dressed in expansive <w>crinolines</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A coarse, stiff fabric made of horsehair combined with cotton or linen, used to line and shape garments.

examples.text: The tailor used heavy <w>crinoline</w> to give the collar and lapels additional structure.
Originally, <w>crinoline</w> was prized by dressmakers for its natural stiffness and durability.

senses.sense_definition: One of the structural hoops forming the supporting framework for cladding over a steam boiler.

examples.text: The engineer secured each <w>crinoline</w> around the boiler before applying the outer insulation.
Workers inspected the steel <w>crinoline</w> for cracks prior to reinstalling the locomotive cladding.

senses.sense_definition: A protective framework of wire netting hung around a warship to detonate or deflect torpedoes.

examples.text: The battleship deployed its <w>crinoline</w> while anchored in the harbor to deter submarine attacks.
Naval commanders soon abandoned the steel <w>crinoline</w> because it reduced the ship's speed too severely.
